author: WP15
summary: Storage chapter updated for the Bible pin: device contract, root resolution, container operations, containment, the untested glob, ignored FileShare and the exception boundary. Its root chain (SDL_GetPrefPath first) and its claim that tests cover ordinary read/write are wrong at TARGET. The Storage guide and the very deep storage internals page already carried nearly everything; complete-read guidance, exact wildcard semantics and disposal/sharing consequences were added to the guide as an expansion.

sections.heading: Path containment and the remaining glob gap

concepts.text: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Storage maps XNA's device-selection API onto one local filesystem root with real save operations and path containment; it is a local filesystem abstraction, not an authorisation or cloud-save boundary.
tokens: StorageContainer maps to a real directory on the local filesystem

concepts.text: StorageDevice reports FreeSpace and TotalSpace from the filesystem and an IsConnected flag.
The Storage Begin*/End* pairs keep XNA's asynchronous shape but complete synchronously: the callback has run before Begin returns.
Selector overloads accept player, free-space and directory-count constraints; the size and count constraints are ignored because there is no removable-device choice.
tokens: the size and count arguments are accepted and ignored

concepts.text: StorageDevice::DeviceChanged is declared for source compatibility and never raised.
SetAppNameEXT selects the per-application root and invalidates the cached resolution, so it must be called before storage or GamerServices access; GetStorageRootEXT exposes the resolved path.
Ownership is explicit: EndShowSelector returns std::unique_ptr<StorageDevice> and EndOpenContainer returns std::unique_ptr<StorageContainer>.
The storage root is resolved lazily on first use and cached until SetAppNameEXT changes the application name.

Claimed resolution order SDL_GetPrefPath, then XDG_DATA_HOME, HOME/.local/share and the working directory: at the snapshot SDL is not used; the order is Android's isolated root, XDG_DATA_HOME, LOCALAPPDATA, HOME (Library/Application Support on Apple, .local/share elsewhere), then the working directory.
concepts.note: Not copied; the Storage guide already documents the TARGET chain.

concepts.text: The final working-directory fallback depends on where the process was started and is not a stable save location.
If the root does not exist, the space queries return LLONG_MAX (at the snapshot the root is created on first resolution, so this arises only if it later disappears).
tokens: LLONG_MAX when the root does not exist

concepts.text: IsConnected walks up to the first existing ancestor of the root, so true does not prove that the per-application directory exists; it is not removable-media detection.
tokens: walks up to the nearest existing ancestor

concepts.text: StorageContainer provides create, delete, existence, enumeration and wildcard-pattern operations for files and directories; OpenFile returns a System::IO::Stream; paths are relative to the container.
StorageContainer::Dispose is idempotent, sets IsDisposed and raises Disposing, but does not guard later operations: treat a disposed container as unusable even though path operations still work.
tokens: no file or directory method checks the flag

target.evidence: modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp (Dispose; no isDisposed_ checks in operations)

concepts.text: The container keeps a non-owning const StorageDevice*, so the device must outlive it.
tokens: The only use of the borrowed device pointer is getStorageDeviceProperty
concepts.note: The internals page is sharper: every file operation uses the captured path, so only getStorageDeviceProperty needs the device alive.

target.evidence: modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp (getStorageDeviceProperty is the only device_ use)

concepts.section: Path containment and the remaining glob gap
concepts.text: Device and container route untrusted names through the core containment helpers: empty and absolute/rooted paths are refused, normalised '..' must stay below the root, existing symlinks are checked through a canonical path used for validation only; 'saves/../profiles' is accepted, an outside traversal or symlink escape throws std::invalid_argument.

concepts.section: Path containment and the remaining glob gap
concepts.text: Snapshot tests cover opening and deleting containers, file and directory operations, traversal, absolute paths, in-root normalisation and symlink escape.

concepts.section: Path containment and the remaining glob gap
concepts.text: The pattern overloads use a hand-written matcher in which '*' matches any sequence and '?' one character (one byte), everything else literal and case-sensitive.

concepts.section: Path containment and the remaining glob gap
concepts.text: The storage tests prove containment but do not exercise the matcher's edge cases (empty matches, literal dots, Unicode names, multiple wildcards, long names); complex patterns are source-proven only.

The four-argument OpenFile accepts System::IO::FileShare but discards it and constructs FileStream with path, mode and access only; without a share-mode constructor or cross-process locking, None, Read and ReadWrite behave identically.
Do not use FileShare::None as protection against concurrent save writers; serialise saves in the game.
tokens: Do not rely on it to keep two writers apart

concepts.text: StorageDeviceNotConnectedException is thrown when the space queries translate a filesystem exception, and also when the root cannot be created on first use.
tokens: Unable to create the storage directory.
concepts.note: Adds the root-creation throw the claim omitted.

concepts.text: Container and file operations neither check IsConnected first nor translate host errors into StorageDeviceNotConnectedException; I/O errors and bad paths surface as other exceptions.
tokens: ordinary I/O errors and bad paths surface as other exceptions

concepts.text: Claim that snapshot tests establish ordinary read/write behaviour: no C++ storage test writes bytes through a container and reads them back (only the C ABI smoke test does, in C ABI builds).
tokens: there is still no test that writes bytes through a container and reads them back

issues.text: StorageContainer path operations had no containment check (fs::path(storagePath_) / relative), letting '../' or absolute paths escape the container.
issues.evidence: modules/storage/src/StorageContainer.cpp (constructor ResolveContainedPath; ResolveNativePath -> ResolveContainedNativePathFromBase for every path method); StorageDeviceTests.cpp (ContainerOperationsRejectLexicalEscapes, ContainerOperationsRejectSymlinkEscapes, ContainerOpenRejectsPathsOutsideStorageRoot)

issues.text: The hand-written GlobMatch behind GetFileNames(pattern)/GetDirectoryNames(pattern) has no test of its semantics (empty matches, literal dots, non-ASCII names, multiple wildcards, long names).
StorageContainer::OpenFile discards its FileShare argument; FileStream has no share mode and no cross-process lock, so FileShare::None does not exclude other writers.
No C++ storage test writes bytes through a StorageContainer stream and reads them back; only the C ABI smoke test (C ABI builds only) does.
StorageContainer methods keep working after Dispose (no disposed check); XNA's behaviour after disposal was not checked here.
Under Emscripten no persistent filesystem is mounted (no IDBFS/syncfs in the tree), so storage and the GamerServices store are lost on page reload.
issues.evidence: grep of TARGET tree (excluding third_party/vendor) for IDBFS|syncfs|FS.mount: no hits

issues.text: Container and file operations do not translate host errors into StorageDeviceNotConnectedException (only root creation and space queries do); documented boundary.
